name: novice-understands
note: Brand new (no years, no projects) but understands the basics.

name: advanced-beginner
note: A year of practice; can apply the basics.

name: competent
note: Three shipped projects; can analyse at the competent level.

name: proficient-with-a-slip
note: Six years; one careless miss on a proficient C4 item should not drag the placement down.

name: expert
note: Twelve years and 25 projects; creates at the expert level.

name: over-claimer
note: EDGE CASE for review. Claims expert experience but only knows advanced beginner C3. 12 items walk down at most 3 cells from expert C5, so the learner is never tested at their level; the rules then fall back to novice C1 at low confidence. The first checkpoint's auto-correction (master §12) is the safety net.

name: silent-expert
note: EDGE CASE for review. A real expert who skips the self-report starts at novice C1 and climbs one cell per batch (estimates 1, 2, 3), so 12 items are only ever tested up to advanced beginner C3, which is where the placement lands. The self-report matters.
